name: 66 German
description: 66 German (Sechsundsechzig): two-player trick-taking. 24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9). 6 cards each; turned card for trump. First to 66 trick points (and declare) wins the hand. Marriages (K+Q same suit) 20 or 40; close stock to force follow suit. Game to 7 match points.

history.origins: German two-player game (Sechsundsechzig); said to originate around 1652 in Paderborn. Related to Schnapsen (Austria).
timeline: 1652: Tradition holds that Sixty-Six (Sechsundsechzig) was first played in Paderborn, Westphalia, where a commemorative plaque now marks the site.
19th century: Documented in German card-game compendia as a shortened 24-card Mariage variant that allows a player to go out on reaching 66 points.
20th century: Becomes a staple two-player tavern game across Germany, while the closely related Schnapsen variant gains national-game status in Austria.

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 2
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: None (two-player duel)
setup.deck:
Type: Standard 24-card pack made by removing 2–8 from a French- or German-suited deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9 in each of four suits).
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
setup.dealing:
Cards per Player: 6
Dealing Pattern: Dealer shuffles and deals 6 cards to each player (in packets or singly), then turns the next card face up to set the trump suit and places the remaining 11 cards crosswise on top as the stock (talon).
setup.equipment:
24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9 in four suits)
Score markers or sevens/eights for game points
Table space

rules.objective: Be first to 66 trick points in a hand (and declare) or reach 7 match points.
rules.gameplay: 6 cards each; trump from turn-up. Play tricks; marriages 20/40; close stock to force follow suit. First to 66 and declare wins hand; 7 match points wins game.

strategy.basic: Declare marriages when safe; close stock when you can make 66.
strategy.intermediate: Count trick points; hold trump 9 (nine of trumps) for key tricks.
strategy.advanced: When to exchange turn-up for 9; force follow by closing stock.
tips: Stock closed = must follow suit when possible.

variations.name: Three-player 66
variations.description: Three-handed game in which all 24 cards are dealt out, eight to each player. One player chooses trumps from an initial three-card packet, there is no talon, players must follow suit and try to win tricks, and marriages still score 20 or 40 while the aim remains to reach 66 card points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This three-player deal and scoring structure is documented from sources, but engine-level overrides for player count, deal pattern, and trick flow have not yet been parameterized.

variations.name: Four-player partnership 66
variations.description: Partnership variant where two teams of two play with a 24-card pack and aim for 66 points as a side. Sources describe adjusted dealing, trump selection, and partnership scoring but retain the same marriage and trick-point structure as the base game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Partnership seating, scoring, and any special contracts are captured narratively; concrete engine overrides for team structure and scoring aggregation are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Trick points (A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0); marriages 20 or 40. First to 66 wins hand; game to 7.
